baseline.scope: Loopback OpenSSH through real gVisor PTY; direct connection versus retained canonical interpreter and native projection. Includes client headless parsing, excludes Warp/browser GUI paint and WAN latency. Throughput uses source payload bytes; projected SSH bytes can differ. Latency ends at parsed acknowledgement, not the polling interval.
baseline.failure: Retained SSH disconnected during the initial unthrottled 2 MiB payload; the completion marker was not delivered.

environment.kernel_note: Same fixed locally built kernel and materialized runtime used for both. Kernel contains concurrent development changes; this isolates the package version comparison but is not a reproduction of the deployed machine.

sshBaseline.scope: Real loopback OpenSSH, authenticated kernel, gVisor PTY, retained interpreter and VT projection; parsed client display, excluding GUI paint and WAN latency

sshCurrent.scope: Real loopback OpenSSH, authenticated kernel, gVisor PTY, retained interpreter and VT projection; parsed client display, excluding GUI paint and WAN latency

browserBaseline.scope: Real Chromium production terminal mount, authenticated retained WebSocket and gVisor PTY. Public xterm onWriteParsed and onRender hooks record receipt versus renderer completion; excludes physical monitor scanout and WAN latency.

browserCurrent.scope: Real Chromium production terminal mount, authenticated retained WebSocket and gVisor PTY. Public xterm onWriteParsed and onRender hooks record receipt versus renderer completion; excludes physical monitor scanout and WAN latency.

extendedComparison.quantiles: Raw quantiles use nearest rank; the summary SSH table uses the conventional median of the retained raw latency samples.
notes: The parsedMs fields in earlier exploratory browser throughput records were not reliable and are excluded; final browser throughput measures onRender completion.
A zero renderUpdates count is expected during idle workloads and indicates starvation only during the independently verified continuing frame workload.
